title: Bekasi Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Bekasi Marathon 2026 Review: Course, Heat, Cut-offs, Finish Times
meta_description: Bekasi Marathon 2026 review: flat Harapan Indah roads, 25°C at the 4am start and 31°C by the cut-off, six-hour marathon limit, and how fast the 1,626 finishers ran.
dek: What the 9 August 2026 race in Kota Harapan Indah was like: the flat township course, the weather from the 4am start to the 10am cut-off, the cut-offs and how close the field came to them, and how fast you need to be to place.
verdict: Enter if you want a flat, low-key race on the eastern edge of Jakarta with a small enough field to place in. The 2026 race had 155 marathon, 580 half-marathon and 891 10 km finishers on the roads of Kota Harapan Indah. The marathon started at 4am in 25°C air with 83% humidity, but it was 29°C by 9am and 31°C at the 10am cut-off, so anyone slower than about four and a half hours ran the last hour in real heat. The six-hour marathon limit is an hour longer than in 2025, and half the marathon field finished after 4:50. Learn the turns: the course winds through a large housing township, and a marathoner went more than a kilometre off route in 2024.

sections.heading: The Course: Flat Roads Through a Housing Township
paragraphs: The race starts and finishes in Kota Harapan Indah, a large housing and shophouse township on the Bekasi side of the Jakarta border, around the Sayana Apartment area in Pusaka Rakyat, Tarumajaya [1]. All four distances stay inside the township and its approach roads; the organiser published separate route maps for the 5 km, 10 km, half and full marathon [1].

The organiser pitches it as a runner-friendly route for everyone from beginners to runners chasing a personal best, in a green setting [2]. A report on the 2025 race, on the same township roads, described the marathon route as fairly flat and lined with shady trees [3]. There are no hills worth training for; what makes it hard is the heat after sunrise and the number of turns.

sections.heading: The Weather: Mild Before Dawn, Hot by the Cut-off
paragraphs: Halim Perdanakusuma airport, about 13 km south-west of the start, recorded 25°C at 4am on race morning, with a dew point of 22°C, 83% humidity and a 3-knot wind [4]. It cooled slightly before dawn, to 24°C at 5am, when the half marathon started, and 23°C with 94% humidity at 6am [4].

Then it heated up fast. It was 27°C at 8am, 29°C at 9am and 31°C with 55% humidity at 10am, when the marathon closed [4]. A three-hour marathoner was finished at 7am, before the worst of it; a five-hour runner did the last hour in 27°C to 29°C sunshine, and the slowest ran into the 30s.

The date matters. The 2025 race was held in February, in the rainy season, and runners were rained on at the start [3]. The move to August puts the race in the dry season, which means less rain and more sun once it comes up.

sections.heading: Cut-offs and Finisher Items
paragraphs: In 2026 the marathon started at 4am with a six-hour limit, the half marathon at 5am with three and a half hours, the 10 km at 5.45am with two hours and the 5 km at 6am with an hour and a half [5]. That is more generous than in 2025, when the race director named the five-hour marathon and three-hour half-marathon cut-offs as the event's main challenge [3].

The longer limits caught almost nobody. Six of the 155 marathon finishers (4%) crossed the line after six hours of gun time, and another 15 came in during the last quarter of an hour. In the half, five of 580 finishers were outside three and a half hours; in the 10 km, three of 891 were outside two hours [6].
Every finisher got a medal, and marathon finishers also got a finisher jacket, alongside the race jersey in the pack [1].

sections.heading: Finding Your Way
paragraphs: A route that loops round a township has a lot of corners. At the 2024 race, held in the same township, a marathoner said she went about one and a half kilometres off course after losing concentration, and asked for clearer direction signs and a marshal at every turn [7]. In a marathon field of only 155 you may run long stretches alone, so study the route map before race day, especially for the second half.

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The official results list 155 marathon, 580 half-marathon and 891 10 km finishers; the 5 km is not included [6]. All times below are gun times.

The marathon was won in 2:56:34, and the top ten finished between 2:56 and 3:40. The median finisher took 4:49:58; 21% broke four hours, 61% broke five, and 90% were home by 5:49:34. Only nine marathon finishers were women, 6% of the field, and the fastest of them ran 2:57:49 [6].

In the half marathon the top ten ran 1:15:39 to 1:33:52, the median was 2:27:32, 13% broke two hours and 55% broke two and a half; 90% were done by 3:05:37. Women were 13% of half-marathon finishers [6].
The 10 km was the biggest race. The top ten ran 32:53 to 39:28, the median was 1:16:01, 17% broke an hour, and 29% of finishers were women [6].
With so few marathoners, a 3:40 run would have made the top ten, and the organiser offered prizes to the top three men and women in each category [1].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: The organiser is CEO Runners. Race packs were collected on Friday and Saturday, 7 and 8 August [2]. The 2026 entry fees were Rp350,000 for the 5 km, Rp450,000 for the 10 km, Rp660,000 for the half marathon and Rp900,000 for the marathon, with a jersey, bib and finisher medal included [5]. The organiser planned for around 5,000 runners across the four distances [1].
Kota Harapan Indah is on the north-eastern edge of greater Jakarta. For a 4am start, staying in or near the township, or arranging a car, is simpler than relying on public transport at that hour.

sections.heading: Should You Enter the Next Bekasi Marathon?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a flat, uncrowded race close to Jakarta, a realistic shot at a top-ten place in the marathon, or a first half marathon with a generous three-and-a-half-hour limit. Half the half-marathon field finished after 2:28, so slower runners have plenty of company.

Think twice if you need a marathon below 4:30 in cool air, or you dislike running alone: the marathon field is small, and anything beyond about 7.30am is run in rising heat. Check the next date and whether the race stays in August, which is drier but hotter than the February date of 2025.
This review draws on the organiser's and listing sites' race information, local reporting on the 2024 and 2025 races, airport weather records and the official results.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the Bekasi Marathon?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the limits were six hours for the marathon, three and a half hours for the half marathon, two hours for the 10 km and an hour and a half for the 5 km. That is an hour longer for the marathon than in 2025. Only 4% of marathon finishers and under 1% of half-marathon finishers came in outside the limit.

faqs.question: What time does the Bekasi Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Early. In 2026 the marathon started at 4am, the half marathon at 5am, the 10 km at 5.45am and the 5 km at 6am, all in Kota Harapan Indah. The early starts beat the heat for faster runners: it was 25°C at 4am but 29°C by 9am and 31°C by the 10am marathon cut-off.

faqs.question: Is the Bekasi Marathon course flat?
faqs.answer: Yes. The race loops through the roads of Kota Harapan Indah township, and a report on the 2025 edition described the marathon route as fairly flat and lined with shady trees. The difficulty is heat after sunrise and the number of turns: at the 2024 race a marathoner went about 1.5 km off course.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to place at the Bekasi Marathon?
faqs.answer: Not very fast in the marathon. In 2026 the top ten marathoners ran between 2:56 and 3:40, and only nine of the 155 finishers were women. The half-marathon top ten ran 1:16 to 1:34 and the 10 km top ten 32:53 to 39:28. The median marathoner finished in 4:50.
